name: Alabama
trivia: The University of Alabama's Crimson Tide football program has captured 18 recognized national championships.
UAB's medical center is one of the largest academic medical centers in the U.S. and the state's largest single employer.

name: Alaska
trivia: The University of Alaska Fairbanks runs one of the world's most active auroral research programs and even operates its own rocket range.
Alaska's public university system was chartered in 1917 as the Alaska Agricultural College and School of Mines — decades before Alaska became a state.

name: Arizona
trivia: Arizona State University in Tempe is the largest public university in the U.S. by on-campus enrollment, with over 145,000 students.
The University of Arizona's Lunar and Planetary Laboratory has led more NASA planetary missions than any other public university.

name: Arkansas
trivia: The University of Arkansas houses the Clinton School of Public Service — the only school in the U.S. offering a Master of Public Service degree.
The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences is the state's only academic health center and one of the top rural-health training programs in the country.

name: California
trivia: Stanford University alumni have founded companies whose combined revenue would rank as one of the world's largest economies.
Caltech has produced more Nobel laureates per capita than any other university in the world.

name: Colorado
trivia: CU Boulder is home to five Nobel laureates and one of the largest university-based space research programs in the world.
The Colorado School of Mines is one of the world's leading applied-science schools focused on the earth's energy and mineral resources.

name: Connecticut
trivia: Yale University, founded in 1701, is the third-oldest institution of higher education in the U.S. and holds one of the world's largest academic libraries.
The University of Connecticut women's basketball program has won more NCAA championships than any other program in Division I history.

name: Delaware
trivia: The University of Delaware, chartered in 1743, counts three signers of the Declaration of Independence among its earliest students.
Delaware State University is one of the nation's oldest historically Black land-grant universities, founded in 1891.

name: Florida
trivia: Gatorade was invented at the University of Florida in 1965 to keep the Gators football team hydrated in the Florida heat.
The University of Miami's Rosenstiel School is the only academic oceanographic institution in the continental U.S. with a private island research site.

name: Georgia
trivia: Georgia Tech's engineering program is consistently ranked among the top ten in the world — former President Jimmy Carter is one of its most famous alumni.
Emory University shares its Atlanta campus with the CDC and runs one of the largest medical research operations in the American South.

name: Hawaii
trivia: The University of Hawaii at Mānoa runs one of only a handful of U.S. astronomy programs with observatories atop Mauna Kea, among the world's premier sky-viewing sites.
The University of Hawaii system was originally chartered in 1907 as a land-grant college of agriculture and mechanic arts.

name: Idaho
trivia: The University of Idaho was the first land-grant university in the Pacific Northwest, chartered in 1889 — a year before Idaho became a state.
Boise State University's blue turf, installed in 1986, was the first non-green football field in the world and remains one of only a handful.

name: Illinois
trivia: The University of Chicago has produced 100 Nobel laureates — more per capita than any other university in the world.
Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management is one of the world's top-ranked business schools and a pioneer of nonprofit management education.

name: Indiana
trivia: Notre Dame's iconic Golden Dome atop the main building is coated in real 23-karat gold leaf, replaced roughly every 15 to 20 years.
Purdue University has trained more astronauts than any other public university, including Neil Armstrong and Gus Grissom.

name: Iowa
trivia: The Iowa Writers' Workshop at the University of Iowa was the first creative-writing MFA program in the world and has produced 17 Pulitzer Prize winners.
Iowa State University pioneered the Atanasoff-Berry Computer, widely credited as the first electronic digital computer.

name: Kansas
trivia: The first basketball coach at the University of Kansas was James Naismith — the man who invented the game.
Kansas State University in Manhattan was the nation's first operational land-grant college under the 1862 Morrill Act.

name: Kentucky
trivia: The University of Kentucky men's basketball program holds the most wins in NCAA Division I history.
Centre College in Danville has produced two U.S. vice presidents, two Supreme Court justices, and 13 senators despite an undergraduate enrollment of fewer than 1,500.

name: Louisiana
trivia: Tulane University's medical school was the first in the Deep South, founded in 1834 to combat yellow-fever outbreaks in New Orleans.
Xavier University of Louisiana is the only historically Black Catholic university in the U.S. and consistently sends more African American students to medical school than any other institution.

name: Maine
trivia: Bowdoin College counts Nathaniel Hawthorne, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, and President Franklin Pierce among its 19th-century alumni.
Together with Bates and Colby, Bowdoin forms Maine's CBB liberal-arts consortium — three of the top-ranked small colleges in the country.

name: Maryland
trivia: Johns Hopkins was America's first research university (1876) and consistently leads U.S. universities in total research spending.
The U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis has commissioned every officer graduating since 1845 directly into the Navy or Marine Corps.

name: Massachusetts
trivia: Harvard University, founded in 1636, is the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States and holds the world's largest academic library.
MIT's endowment supports more Nobel laureates per capita than nearly any other university and drives one of the world's largest research operations.

name: Michigan
trivia: The University of Michigan's Big House is the largest college football stadium in America, seating over 107,000 fans.
Michigan State University was one of the pioneer land-grant institutions of the 1862 Morrill Act and helped shape the entire American public-university model.

name: Minnesota
trivia: University of Minnesota researchers invented the retractable seat belt, the implantable cardiac pacemaker, and the flight data recorder.
Carleton College produces one of the highest per-capita rates of future PhDs among all U.S. undergraduate institutions.

name: Mississippi
trivia: The University of Mississippi (Ole Miss) is home to the National Center for Physical Acoustics, one of the world's leading acoustics research centers.
Mississippi State's Raspet Flight Research Laboratory runs one of the largest university-based unmanned aerial systems programs in the U.S.

name: Missouri
trivia: Washington University in St. Louis has produced 25 Nobel laureates and is consistently ranked among the top medical schools in the U.S.
The University of Missouri, founded in 1839, was the first public university established west of the Mississippi River.

name: Montana
trivia: The University of Montana in Missoula opened one of the earliest Schools of Forestry in the American West, admitting its first students in 1913.
Montana Tech in Butte is one of the nation's premier mining and petroleum-engineering schools and reports one of the highest starting salaries of any public university.

name: Nebraska
trivia: The University of Nebraska–Lincoln football program set the longest home-sellout streak in college football history — 375 consecutive games.
Creighton University's health-sciences campus is home to one of the country's most respected Jesuit medical schools, founded in 1892.

name: Nevada
trivia: UNLV's Harrah College of Hospitality is consistently ranked the top hospitality school in the world.
UNR is one of the oldest land-grant universities in the Mountain West, founded in 1874 — the second-oldest continuously operating public university west of the Rockies.

name: New Hampshire
trivia: Dartmouth College is the smallest school in the Ivy League and the ninth-oldest college in the U.S., founded in 1769 by a charter from King George III.
Phillips Exeter Academy is one of the oldest and most selective boarding schools in the world, with alumni including Facebook co-founder Mark Zuckerberg.

name: New Jersey
trivia: Princeton University's Firestone Library is the largest open-stack academic library in the world, holding more than 13 million volumes.
Rutgers University in New Brunswick is one of only nine colonial colleges chartered before the American Revolution.

name: New Mexico
trivia: Los Alamos National Laboratory, born from the Manhattan Project, remains one of the world's largest multidisciplinary research institutions.
New Mexico Tech operates the Very Large Array radio telescope, one of the most iconic astronomical research facilities in the world.

name: New York
trivia: Columbia University administers the Pulitzer Prize each year and counts more than 100 Nobel laureates among its alumni and faculty.
Cornell University in Ithaca is the only Ivy that combines private and land-grant statutory colleges under one campus.

name: North Carolina
trivia: The Research Triangle links Duke, UNC-Chapel Hill, and NC State — the largest research park in the U.S. by land area.
UNC-Chapel Hill, chartered in 1789, was the first public university in the United States to hold classes and award degrees.

name: North Dakota
trivia: The University of North Dakota was the first American university to offer a fully accredited four-year aviation degree program.
North Dakota State's agricultural research programs helped develop many of the wheat and durum varieties that dominate the northern Great Plains today.

name: Ohio
trivia: Ohio State University enrolls over 60,000 undergraduates and its marching band is the largest all-brass band in the world.
The University of Cincinnati invented cooperative education (co-op) in 1906 — a model now used by universities around the world.

name: Oklahoma
trivia: The University of Oklahoma's Sam Noble Museum houses the largest Apatosaurus skeleton ever mounted for public display.
Oklahoma State University runs one of the leading equine reproduction and veterinary programs in the American Southwest.

name: Oregon
trivia: The University of Oregon is where Nike founder Phil Knight and coach Bill Bowerman first tested the running shoes that grew into the Nike brand.
Reed College has produced 32 Rhodes Scholars, and Apple co-founder Steve Jobs credited its calligraphy class with inspiring Macintosh typography.

name: Pennsylvania
trivia: The University of Pennsylvania was founded by Benjamin Franklin in 1740 and is home to the Wharton School — the world's first collegiate business school.
Carnegie Mellon in Pittsburgh built the first computer science department in the U.S. and remains one of the world's leading AI and robotics research universities.

name: Rhode Island
trivia: Brown University's Open Curriculum lets undergraduates choose any courses they want with no core requirements — unique among the Ivies.
The Rhode Island School of Design shares a Providence campus with Brown and is one of the top-ranked art and design schools in the world.

name: South Carolina
trivia: Clemson University was founded on land bequeathed by Thomas Green Clemson, son-in-law of Vice President John C. Calhoun.
The Citadel in Charleston is one of only six senior military colleges in the U.S., commissioning graduates directly into any branch of the armed services.

name: South Dakota
trivia: The South Dakota School of Mines & Technology reports the highest starting-salary rate for graduates of any public university in the U.S.
The University of South Dakota, chartered in 1862, was established before South Dakota became a state and remains the state's oldest university.

name: Tennessee
trivia: Vanderbilt University was founded with a $1 million gift from railroad magnate Cornelius Vanderbilt — the only philanthropic donation of his lifetime.
Oak Ridge National Laboratory, co-managed by the University of Tennessee, is the largest science and energy national lab in the U.S.

name: Texas
trivia: The University of Texas at Austin has one of the ten largest university endowments in the world and one of the largest single-campus enrollments in the country.
Rice University in Houston has one of the highest endowment-per-student ratios in the U.S. and is one of the smallest R1 research universities.

name: Utah
trivia: Brigham Young University offers instruction in more than 60 languages — the most of any undergraduate university in the U.S.
The University of Utah's computer graphics program in the 1970s produced founders of Pixar, Adobe, Silicon Graphics, and Netscape.

name: Vermont
trivia: Middlebury College's Language Schools are so intensive that students take an oath to speak only their studied language for the entire summer.
Norwich University, founded in 1819, is the oldest private military college in the United States and the birthplace of the ROTC concept.

name: Virginia
trivia: The University of Virginia was founded and designed by Thomas Jefferson in 1819 — he considered it one of his three greatest life achievements.
William & Mary, chartered in 1693, is the second-oldest college in the U.S. and has educated three of America's first ten presidents.

name: Washington
trivia: The University of Washington runs one of the largest medical research operations of any public university in the world.
Washington State's Bear Research Center is the only university-based facility in the U.S. permitted to study grizzly bears in captivity.

name: West Virginia
trivia: West Virginia University in Morgantown operates the world's longest fully automated Personal Rapid Transit system, connecting three of its campuses.
Marshall University's Forensic Science Center is one of the largest university-based forensic training programs in the country and works closely with the FBI.

name: Wisconsin
trivia: Vitamins A and B were both isolated by researchers at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in the early 20th century.
Marquette University in Milwaukee is one of the largest Jesuit universities in America and home to one of only two dental schools in Wisconsin.

name: Wyoming
trivia: The University of Wyoming is the only four-year public university in the state and guarantees scholarship consideration to every Wyoming high-school graduate.
Founded in 1886, the University of Wyoming is one of the few land-grant universities established while its territory had not yet become a state.

name: Alberta
trivia: The University of Alberta in Edmonton is one of Canada's top research universities and has produced Nobel laureates and Rhodes Scholars.
Athabasca University is Canada's premier open online university and pioneered distance learning in the country long before the internet age.

name: British Columbia
trivia: The University of British Columbia sits on a 1,000-acre oceanfront campus in Vancouver and consistently ranks among the top 40 universities in the world.
Simon Fraser University in Burnaby was Canada's first university built as a single, unified architectural work — designed by Arthur Erickson.

name: Manitoba
trivia: The University of Manitoba, founded in 1877, was the first university established in Western Canada.
The University of Winnipeg operates one of Canada's most extensive Indigenous studies programs and offers reduced tuition to Indigenous students from Manitoba.

name: New Brunswick
trivia: The University of New Brunswick, founded in 1785, is the oldest English-language university in Canada and the third-oldest in North America.
Mount Allison University in Sackville has produced more Rhodes Scholars per capita than any other university in Canada.

name: Newfoundland and Labrador
trivia: Memorial University in St. John's was founded to memorialize Newfoundlanders killed in the World Wars and remains Atlantic Canada's largest university.
Memorial's Marine Institute is one of the world's leading centers for fisheries, marine engineering, and Arctic ocean research.

name: Nova Scotia
trivia: Dalhousie University in Halifax is home to one of the world's leading ocean research programs, powered by its Atlantic-coast location.
Nova Scotia has more universities per capita than any other Canadian province, packing 10 universities into a province of under 1 million people.

name: Northwest Territories
trivia: Aurora College operates the territory's post-secondary system with campuses in Yellowknife, Fort Smith, and Inuvik.
The Aurora Research Institute in Inuvik has studied the aurora borealis and Arctic permafrost for more than 50 years.

name: Nunavut
trivia: Nunavut Arctic College is the territory's only post-secondary institution and delivers programs in both English and Inuktitut.
The college's Nunavut Teacher Education Program has trained the majority of Inuit teachers in Nunavut over the past three decades.

name: Ontario
trivia: Insulin was discovered at the University of Toronto in 1921 — a breakthrough that earned the university a Nobel Prize the following year.
McMaster University pioneered problem-based learning in medical education, a model now used by medical schools around the world.

name: Prince Edward Island
trivia: The University of Prince Edward Island is home to the Atlantic Veterinary College — one of only five veterinary schools in all of Canada.
UPEI is the smallest comprehensive university in Canada by enrollment but consistently ranks among the top primarily-undergraduate universities in the country.

name: Quebec
trivia: McGill University, founded in 1821 by fur trader James McGill, is consistently ranked among the top universities in the world.
Université Laval in Quebec City, founded in 1663, is the oldest French-language university in North America.

name: Saskatchewan
trivia: The University of Saskatchewan led the development of canola oil in the 1970s — one of Canada's most successful agricultural innovations.
The University of Regina hosts the First Nations University of Canada, the only First Nations-controlled degree-granting institution in the country.

name: Yukon
trivia: Yukon University became Canada's first university north of 60° in 2020, with programs deeply shaped by the territory's Indigenous cultures.
Yukon University's Cold Climate Research Centre is one of Canada's leading facilities for northern permafrost, mining, and climate-change research.
